claims.statement: SaiLoR has three deliberately separated test tiers: Vitest unit tests (the default, fastest tier, run on every PR), a jsdom integration suite that mocks the platform seam and spins up real scratch git repos (slower, kept off the default run), and Playwright/Electron e2e smoke tests for the real main process / contextBridge / IPC.

The Vitest unit tier is configured in the test block of vite.config.ts with environment jsdom, globals true, include src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}, and an exclude list that explicitly drops *.integration.test.{ts,tsx} (the exclude replaces Vite's default list rather than appending, so the usual node_modules/dist/etc. entries are repeated alongside it).
The unit tier runs via `npm test` (`vitest run`) and `npm run test:watch` (`vitest`), as defined in package.json scripts.

The integration tier uses a standalone config (vitest.integration.config.ts) rather than mergeConfig over vite.config.ts, because Vite's mergeConfig concatenates array fields like test.include instead of replacing them, which would silently pull the ~90 unit test files into the integration run too.
The integration tier runs via `npm run test:integration` (`vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts`) and includes only src/test/integration/**/*.integration.test.tsx.

Integration tests mock getPlatform() to inject a fake PlatformAdapter at that single seam, which makes the whole app run under jsdom without a real Electron environment (the same interface that lets the app run in Electron and in a plain browser).

Each integration test spins up a real scratch git repository per test (mkdtempSync, git init, initial commit) and wires a fake GitPlatform whose status/commit/beginPull/etc. shell out to the real git binary against that directory, so merge/pull/push/branch-switch/discard flows run against genuine git rather than a stub.

Integration tests render the real React components with React Testing Library (render/screen/userEvent) and drive them with real clicks/typing/DOM events, not direct store calls; because jsdom performs no real layout they stub getBoundingClientRect/Range.getClientRects/ResizeObserver and mock react-pdf, but everything above that (selection capture, mark creation, the comment popover, annotation form, Git panel) is the genuine component code.

Integration tests verify outcomes independently of the app by reading the scratch repo directly (e.g. git log -1 --format=%s, git show HEAD:project.json), so a green test proves a real commit landed rather than just that the store claims it did.

The integration suite in src/test/integration/ covers annotationWorkflow (schema authoring, PDF annotation, git commit), consolidationAndMerge, branchSwitch (stash-carry-over field-level conflict), pull (real git pull against a bare origin diverged by a second clone), discard (writeWorking not commit), pdfReadingPosition, and screeningImport.
The e2e tier runs via `npm run test:e2e` which is `cross-env ELECTRON=1 npm run build && playwright test`; it requires ELECTRON=1 and a built app (the script builds dist-electron/main.js first).

The Playwright config is an Electron smoke test for the class of bug jsdom structurally cannot see: the preload bridge and the main process's IPC handlers actually wired up correctly; it deliberately does not duplicate the UI-shaped coverage already in the jsdom integration suite, and runs with workers: 1 because each test launches its own real Electron process with no shared state to race.

The e2e tests drive the window.slr bridge methods directly (openPath, saveProject, gitProbe, gitStatus, gitPush) rather than through the rendered UI, because the native Open/Save dialogs a real user click would hit are exactly what Playwright cannot drive here.

The openSaveProject e2e test exercises a real guard in electron/main.ts's project:save handler that refuses to write to any path not first opened via project:open/openPath (knownProjectPaths); it proves the guard is real by asserting a save to an unopened path is rejected with /was not opened or chosen/, while a save to the previously opened path succeeds and writes through the real IPC handler.

The openSaveProject e2e test is the only one that reaches electron/main.ts's real runGit/gitEnv/GIT_SAFE_CONFIG wrapper (which strips GIT_DIR, disables hooks/pager/ext-diff) through the real contextBridge/IPC path, via gitProbe (available true, version matches /git version/) and gitStatus against a real git directory.

The openSaveProject e2e test is the only test that exercises the real split layout save (project.json carries metadata only; annotations/<id>/*.json holds the per-paper answer) and the reassembly (readProjectText → assembleLegacyProjectJson) a real reopen does to turn the split files back into the single in-memory shape; it confirms project.json stays meta-only (not containing the answer) and the per-paper file holds it.

The gitPush e2e test drives the real git:push IPC handler (plain git push through the hardened runGit wrapper) against a real bare origin, establishes upstream tracking with real git first, then confirms the commit landed by reading the bare repo directly (git log -1 --format=%s in originDir), independent of the app and of the local clone's own idea of what happened.

scripts/ci.sh is the provider-agnostic single source of truth for whether the app builds and passes its checks; CI providers only check out the code, provide a Node toolchain, and run this script, so the same checks run locally with ./scripts/ci.sh. It runs steps in order with set -euo pipefail: typecheck (tsc -b), wiki link check (check:wiki), tests (vitest, unit tier only), and build (vite build).

The CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs ./scripts/ci.sh on ubuntu-latest (Node 24) on every push to main and every pull request, running the unit tier only (npm test excludes integration tests); it is deliberately not triggered on push to every branch to avoid building a branch with an open PR twice.

integration-tests.yml is a reusable workflow (workflow_call + workflow_dispatch) with two jobs: integration-test (npm run test:integration) and e2e-test (xvfb-run -a npm run test:e2e, which needs a real display because Electron opens a real native window on Linux); it stays independently triggerable for a fast check without a full release run.

release.yml (on release published) gates the build job on the integration-tests reusable workflow via needs: integration-tests, so a broken end-to-end workflow (schema authoring, PDF annotation, git commit, merge/pull/branch-switch/discard, screening import, real IPC) is blocked from reaching a packaged release; the build job then builds packaged Electron apps for macOS/Windows/Linux via electron-builder.

Pure model tests in src/model/*.test.ts cover schema resolution (defaults, path ids, duplicate sibling names, enum options, max<min rejection, required defaults), normalizeTree/pruneTree/canAdd/canRemove, and loadProject→serializeProject round-trip, with fixtures built through the real load path (loadProject/serializeProject) so inputs are exactly as schema-normalized as a real file would be.

Store tests (src/state/store.*.test.ts) mock the platform seam at getPlatform() with a kind:'browser' fake PlatformAdapter, use a beforeEach that loads a known project via loadFromText, and cover annotation lifecycle, undo/redo (including coalescing consecutive same-field edits into one step and a new edit clearing the redo stack), marks, reading position, reviewer seats, save/save-as, and the unlockAi session flag.

gitStore.test.ts stubs the full GitPlatform shape and drives runPull's orchestration (dirty guard, pull classification, parse boundary, merge, resolution dialog) through each branch via beginPullResult/finishPullResult, exercising exactly the branch each test means to test.

merge.test.ts in src/git builds base/ours/theirs fixtures through loadProject (the real load path, not hand-assembled Project objects) so each side is exactly as schema-normalized and empty-skeleton-shaped as a file mergeProjects' caller would actually hand it, covering merge3/mergeProjects/applyResolutions/conflictId over repeatable findings and paper-meta fields.

ref.test.ts covers refProblem, the ref/path safety guard that refuses empty refs, option-like refs (--upload-pack=…), control characters, revision syntax (main^, main~1, main:path, main@{1}), and everything git check-ref-format forbids (spaces, ? * [ \ , leading/trailing/double slashes, trailing dot, .lock) at any path level.

Component tests in src/components/*.test.ts test pure helper functions extracted from components directly without rendering (e.g. PaperList's paperIsMarkedDone, GitDialog's mixedDiscardConfirmMessage and isProjectOwnPath, PdfViewer's destinationPoint/markVerticallyVisible/dedupeOverlappingRects, PapersEditor's duplicatePaperIds); the rendered-component coverage lives in the integration suite instead.

paperIsMarkedDone (PaperList) decides the paper-list status dot; in Consolidation the dot must mean 'every numbered reviewer has answered', read from paper.reviews, not 'does paper.annotations have anything' — because adoptUnanimousValues fills paper.annotations just from opening the paper, making annotations presence no longer a signal the consolidator produced.

mixedDiscardConfirmMessage (GitDialog) warns before a commit silently reverts or deletes a Discard row; a PaperChange marked Discard deletes the paper and all its annotation files (consolidated.json, every reviewer-<n>.json), so it is named as '1 paper' (with 'deleted') rather than the badly-underselling '1 field ... reverted', and discard-only mode suppresses this warning because it has its own separate confirm.

Because jsdom has no layout engine, the integration tests give every element a fixed non-zero getBoundingClientRect (800x1000) and Range.getClientRects a 100x20 rect, which is enough for PdfViewer's own width>1 && height>1 filter (rectsForPageRange) to keep selection rects so the real selection-to-highlight code path produces a real mark; ResizeObserver and the CSS Custom Highlight API (used for in-PDF search) are stubbed as unused.

PlatformAdapter (src/platform/adapter.ts) is the platform abstraction for file I/O and PDF loading that the React app talks only to, so the same code runs inside Electron (native dialogs + fs) and in a plain browser (File System Access API / downloads / fetch); it exposes openProject/saveProject/rebasePdfPaths/getPdfSource/needsPdfFolderGrant/grantPdfFolderAccess plus getGit(), and is the single seam integration tests mock.
